deepdive.sec: Aerospace & Defense Precision Engineering / Auto Components

bull_bear.body: Debt-free balance sheet with INR68cr net cash (consol) and ~INR1,000cr liquid investments at parent; Capex self-funded by subsidiary cash flows; Parent liquidity acts as safety net; No dividend specifics given but strong cash generation supports potential payouts.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 100% reliance on imported aerospace-grade raw materials (supply chain/geopolitical risk); Execution risk on Andhra facility timeline (late FY28); Global OEM certification delays; Potential lag in passing through raw material cost inflation; Concentration in engine components (75%) though diversified across OEMs.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasizes 'derisking' customer base and moving up value chain; Transparent about one-offs (land gain, interest income shift); Modular growth approach to capex (machinery ordered quarterly based on ramp-up) rather than big-bang; Long-term optimism on India's role in global aerospace supply chain.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The flat consolidated EBITDA is an accounting artifact of the Realty demerger (loss of interest income on INR600cr cash transfer), masking a actual ~20% operational EBITDA growth; The company is transitioning from a job-shop model to a 'co-design' partner (build-to-spec), which fundamentally changes valuation multiples; Machinery procurement is continuous and modular (every quarter) to match SKU ramp-up, avoiding large single-point capex risks.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash surplus of ₹68 Cr (FY26), with a dedicated slide headed "Raymond Limited to Remain Net Cash Surplus".
- "Zero Non-Core asset distraction. Capital management bandwidth and cash flows are now 100% dedicated to precision engineering compounding."
- The demerged Raymond Lifestyle is described as having an "Independent Capital Structure"; the deck states no dividend, buyback or leverage policy for Raymond Limited.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Aerospace (JKMGL): Rev INR119cr Q4 (+11%), Margin 25.5%; Full Year Rev INR392cr (+26%), Margin 22.3%. Auto/Precision (JKMPT): Rev INR442cr Q4 (+5%), Margin 15.2%; Full Year Rev INR1,667cr (+10%), Margin 13.4% (incl. INR13cr one-off). Corporate: Neutral/Even-steven.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global OEMs face supply chain friction and need derisked, certified Tier 1 partners in India for engine and structural components. | Raymond Ltd | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of China+1 and global aerospace backlog; unique 'build-to-spec' capability and 25% CAGR guidance with visible order book. |
| Rising input costs and logistics blockades impact margins for companies reliant on imported specialty alloys. | Unorganized Precision Machining Peers | loser | Med | Companies without long-term OEM contracts or localization roadmaps will suffer margin compression; Raymond's scale and localization plans provide a moat. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Corporate restructuring is described as complete: Raymond Lifestyle (listed Sep 05, 2024) and Raymond Realty (listed Jul 01, 2025) are demerged and listed, leaving Raymond Limited as a pure-play engineering company with "Zero Non-Core asset distraction".
- Aerospace arm is positioned as "the leading exporter of highly critical Aero engine components" from India and a "Preferred Supplier To top 3 Global Aircraft Engine Manufacturers holding 88% market share", with 25+ global aero components clients and 2 decades of relationships with top OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers.
- The stated moat is qualification lock-in: programmes run [RFQ Bidding] to [Prototype R&D Sample] to [First Article Inspection (FAIR)] to [10-Year Mass Production], and "Once FAIR qualification is achieved, OEM platform switching costs are prohibitive, ensuring zero customer churn".
- Precision Technology & Auto Components is positioned on category leadership, claiming "#1 in India" for Steel Files and for Ring Gears, and "one of India's leading suppliers of high-end precision components" with 7 decades as a Tier-1 supplier and 100+ large customers globally.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] Raymond Lifestyle listed Sep 05, 2024 carrying Branded Textiles & Apparel and Global Garmenting B2B; Raymond Realty listed Jul 01, 2025 carrying Thane land bank development and an MMR asset-light JDA model, described as a "Top-5 Developer in MMR".
- [Legal entities] Aerospace & Defence is operated through JK Maini Global Aerospace Ltd. (the A&D division of erstwhile Maini Precision) and Precision Technology & Auto Components through JK Maini Precision Technology Ltd. (T&H division, RPAL and the Auto division of erstwhile Maini Precision).
- [Defence traction] Mass production of precision components began for a leading defence OEM; formal audit approvals were achieved from a key Indian defence and aerospace OEM; and a maiden build-to-spec order was received from a leading defence aerospace OEM, alongside development of specialised onboard storage systems.
- [Localization programme] On a flagship aircraft localization program the company secured "135 total part awards—with 100 parts actively in serial production and the remaining 35 parts advancing through final First Article Inspection (FAI)".
- [Governance] The deck flags a "Comprehensive upgrade of leadership, governance, and organizational capabilities", with senior management of 30+ years' industry expertise cited for both segments.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Aerospace margins stable at 22-25% despite 100% imported raw materials (Titanium, Inconel); Auto margins expanded 240bps FYoY due to operational synergies, SAP integration, and product mix, partially aided by INR13cr land gain; Near-term pressure expected from raw material inflation but pass-through mechanisms active; Localization of raw materials (6-8 month timeline) identified as key future margin lever.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue CAGR ~25% for Aerospace over next 2 years; Auto margins sustainable at ~13-14% excluding one-offs; Order inflow steady with 250-350 new SKUs/year; Capex INR930cr over 5 years (INR500cr Aero, INR430cr Auto); New Andhra facility commissioning late CY2027 (Q4 FY28) contributing meaningful revenue from FY29.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR2,350cr (Aerospace specific); >10-year visibility on global aircraft backlog; 75% of book tied to engine programs across multiple OEMs (derisked from single platform); RFQ pipeline converting to multi-year contracts.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Migration to 'build-to-spec' (design ownership) vs traditional 'build-to-print'; Expansion into aerostructures, landing gear, and hydraulics (currently 25% of mix); Gas turbine segment exploration; 300-350 new components added annually; Andhra greenfield facility enabling 2x capacity scale.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Raymond's engineering arm delivered resilient double-digit growth in Aerospace (26% FY26) and margin expansion in Auto (13.4% vs 11%), driven by global OEM diversification and operational synergies, while guiding for a transformative INR930cr capex to double capacity via a new Andhra facility by late FY28. The shift from 'build-to-print' to 'build-to-spec' and a record order book provide multi-year visibility despite near-term raw material import dependencies.
